main_issue: Whether Agent D should leave the pitch work to the team or take her laptop and finish her analysis section from home, and with what safeguards.

A-B.evidence: A insisted D leave the laptop (T15, T17); B argued 'Letting her finish it is less risky' (T18); A conceded 'You're right' (T20).

A-C.evidence: A said 'Agent C has a good point' (T13) and pushed D to leave the laptop; C then said letting D try is better (T19); A conceded and set a 10 p.m. check (T20).

A-D.evidence: A told D to leave the laptop (T15) and D refused (T14); A then allowed the laptop with a 10 p.m. upload (T20), and D accepted (T21).

B-C.evidence: B backed D working from home (T7); C questioned it and asked for a plan B (T10, T12); C then said 'Agent B's right' (T19).

B-D.evidence: B: 'that would be a big help' (T7); D agreed to do it tonight (T8); B argued D should be allowed to finish (T16, T18).

C-D.evidence: C doubted D could finish tonight (T10, T12); D insisted (T11); C later said it's better to let D try (T19), and D accepted the 10 p.m. plan (T21).
